title: p(Doom)1 friends-and-family alpha
_facts_this_copy_must_not_break: Windows build ships today (v0.13.0). macOS and Linux are NOT yet released -- say 'this week', do not imply Mac/Linux are downloadable now.
This is an early alpha. Promise rough edges, not polish.
Do NOT point anyone at the in-game F8 bug reporter: it does not transmit (pdoom1 #800).
Do NOT promise leaderboards or scores - remote submission is not live yet (pdoom1 #735).
The game is free and open source, and non-commercial.

copy.linkedin:
I've been building a game about AI safety on my own, and it's now playable — a lower bar than "good", but I'm claiming it anyway.

p(Doom)1 puts you in charge of an AI safety lab. You hire researchers, chase funding, wrangle compute, and try to lower the odds of catastrophe — mostly via meetings, budgets and paperwork. The bureaucracy is the game.

It's an early alpha, built solo, and rough in the places you'd expect. That's the point of putting it out now: I want to know where it's confusing, where it drags, and where it's accidentally fun.

Windows today — macOS and Linux within the week.

Free, open source, non-commercial.

https://pdoom1.com/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=alpha-launch-2026-07-24

Right — the thing I've been quietly building is playable.

p(Doom)1 is a strategy game where you run an AI safety lab: hiring, funding, compute, and a truly heroic amount of bureaucracy between you and saving the world.

It's an early alpha, so it's held together with optimism in places. I'd genuinely love you to play it badly and tell me exactly what confused you — more useful to me than "nice one, mate".

Windows today; Mac and Linux this week. Free, no catch.
